- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often underreacts in next 5–7 days; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent peak, model underestimates rebound; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias for next 7–10 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); apply 0.7–1.2% upward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 0.3–0.7% upward bias to 30d forecast.
- When official event (e.g., policy change, auction) occurs within 3–5 days, model often lags; adjust forecast 0.5–1.0% upward if event is bullish, or downward if bearish, within 3–7 days of event.
